chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'How intense is the grief of women, and how distant is the separation of death; and more intense than all of that is poverty, in which its owner flatters [others], yet is given nothing.'
ai.seo_question: What does the Prophet say is more intense than the grief of women and the separation of death?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) conveys the Prophet’s (peace be upon him) profound insight that destitution is more agonizing than the grief of women or the finality of death, as it compels the proud to humble themselves through flattery (tamallaq) for sustenance, often without success. This highlights the psychological and social humiliation of poverty, a key theme in Shia ethical teachings regarding dignity and self-sufficiency. The comparison underscores how material lack erodes spiritual and social standing more severely than physical separation or emotional sorrow.

en.hubeali: H 14721 – Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-nawfaly, from Al-Sakuny, who has narrated the following:

Abu Abdullahasws has said that the Rasool Allahsaww said: ‘There is nothing more intense than the grief of a woman, nor anything more remote than the separation of the death, and more intense than all of that is poverty. One flatters his companion, who then does not give him anything’. out of 567
en.sarwar: 273. Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-nawfaly, from Al-Sakuny, who has narrated the following: Abu Abdullah (a.s.) has said that the Rasool Allah (saww) said:

‘There is nothing more intense than the grief of a woman, nor anything more remote than the separation of the death, and more intense than all of that is poverty. One flatters his companion, who then does not give him anything’.
